rows.name: Wispr Flow
rows.reason: Official deployment requires cloud transcription/internet on every platform and offers no offline deployment, violating on-device/non-cloud requirements. Optional cloud-storage controls do not remove cloud transcription.

rows.name: VoiceInk
rows.reason: VoiceInk can replace the speak-and-insert workflow on a Mac using downloaded local transcription models. Current documentation requires macOS 15 or later; disable cloud enhancement and check every automatically selected mode.

rows.name: Handy
rows.reason: Handy documents shortcut-driven dictation into the current field with on-computer voice processing, matching local dictation scope. Previously recorded desktop compatibility caveats still apply.

rows.name: Handy
rows.reason: Its shortcut-driven app transcribes on the computer and pastes into the active text field, directly matching on-device, non-cloud dictation.

rows.name: FOSS Voquill
rows.reason: Cursor-inserting dictation and on-device cleanup require no cloud service. Claims were checked only in documentation; software was not run. Evaluate local-model performance on the intended machine.

rows.name: FOSS Voquill
rows.reason: Cross-platform local dictation with optional on-device text cleanup. Cloud APIs are optional; leave them unused. Hardware performance was not tested.

rows.name: Apache OpenWhisk
rows.reason: It executes event-triggered serverless functions; it supplies neither speech recognition nor a dictation interface, so local deployment alone does not meet the need.

rows.name: Superwhisper
rows.reason: Documented local speech models support a ready-to-use dictation workflow. Cloud speech and cloud rewriting transmit data; use local speech with optional rewriting disabled. Model/hardware availability varies.

rows.name: FUTO Voice Input
rows.reason: Android voice input with explicit offline processing documentation. Gboard and Samsung Keyboard are incompatible; use a supported keyboard. Current listing evidence postdates the question.

rows.name: Handy
rows.reason: Straightforward local dictation across the three main desktop platforms. Linux insertion and Wayland shortcuts require configuration; optional custom processing must remain local.

rows.name: Windows Voice Access
rows.reason: Windows Voice Access provides built-in on-device dictation and application control after a one-time language-model download. Initial setup needs internet and language support is constrained; use the Voice Access feature specifically.

rows.name: YazSes
rows.reason: YazSes combines hold-to-talk, CPU-local faster-whisper and focused-app insertion. Default models target English; documented minimum is 4 GB RAM, with separate model downloads and platform considerations.

rows.name: nerd-dictation
rows.reason: nerd-dictation offers Linux dictation through local Vosk and simulated input. Requires Python, Vosk, recording/input-simulation tools, manually bound controls and a desktop-compatible input backend.

rows.name: Apache OpenWhisk
rows.reason: OpenWhisk executes developer-written event functions, supplying application infrastructure rather than dictation. Local deployment is supported; exclusion concerns task scope, not a requirement to use cloud hosting.

rows.name: VoiceInk
rows.reason: Mac dictation with an explicit no-enhancement mode and local speech models. Best suited to Apple Silicon; Intel cloud recommendation is not proof local operation is unsupported. Check automatic mode triggers.

rows.name: Superwhisper
rows.reason: Superwhisper provides system-wide push-to-talk offline desktop transcription using on-device models. Select an on-device configuration; optional cleanup modes and mobile offline behavior were not verified.

rows.name: Wispr Flow
rows.reason: It is Wispr Flow itself; the vendor also says every platform requires internet, so it does not provide the requested on-device alternative.

rows.name: Handy
rows.reason: Local hotkey dictation inserts speech into text fields across three main desktop platforms. Requires local models and microphone/input permissions; model size and hardware affect latency.
